key_people.name: 阿达汗·马杜马罗夫 (Adakhan Madumarov / Адахан Мадумаров)
key_people.title: 党主席 (Party Chairman / Партия жетекчиси)
key_people.title_description: Founder and lifelong party chairman; Kyrgyz historian and lawyer; former Supreme Council member (1995-2005); ran for president in 2011, 2017, and 2021
key_people.description: Kyrgyz nationalist opposition leader born 1965 in Kurshab, Osh Oblast; graduated from Tver State University and Kyrgyz National University; placed second in 2011 presidential election and third in 2017

key_people.name: 伊斯哈克·马萨利耶夫 (Iskhak Masaliev / Исхак Масалиев)
key_people.title: 议会党团主席 (Faction Leader / Фракция жетекчиси)
key_people.title_description: Became leader of the Butun Kyrgyzstan parliamentary faction in the Jogorku Kenesh on 8 May 2024, succeeding Madumarov
key_people.description: Supreme Council deputy and former head of the Communist Party of Kyrgyzstan; took over faction leadership after Madumarov's arrest and resignation

recent_events.title: 2021 parliamentary election: 6 seats won
recent_events.description: Butun Kyrgyzstan won 7.04% of the vote in the 2021 parliamentary election, clearing the 3% threshold and securing 6 seats to become the third-largest party in the Jogorku Kenesh
recent_events.impact: Party entered the Supreme Council for the first time as a major opposition force

recent_events.title: Madumarov lost presidential election to Japarov
recent_events.description: Madumarov was the main challenger to acting president Sadyr Japarov in the 2021 presidential election but was defeated; he refused to accept the results
recent_events.impact: Party moved into outright opposition against the Japarov government

recent_events.title: Madumarov criticised GKNB anti-smuggling campaign
recent_events.description: Madumarov delivered a parliamentary report criticising the GKNB's anti-smuggling battle; GKNB chairman Kamchybek Tashiyev threatened to break his arm and throw him in jail
recent_events.impact: Escalated tensions between the party and security establishment; foreshadowed later prosecution

recent_events.title: Madumarov arrested by Spetsnaz
recent_events.description: Madumarov and his 13-year-old son were arrested by Spetsnaz special forces while walking in central Bishkek, in connection with a 2009 protocol signed in Khujand, Tajikistan
recent_events.impact: Triggered international concern; Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) engaged; opposition accused government of seeking to destroy the party

recent_events.title: Madumarov convicted of treason and fraud
recent_events.description: Pervomaisky District Court of Bishkek found Madumarov guilty of treason and fraud related to a 2009 agreement signed in Khujand, but released him from punishment due to expiration of statute of limitations
recent_events.impact: Madumarov was stripped of his parliamentary mandate; political career effectively ended

recent_events.title: Masaliev replaces Madumarov as faction leader
recent_events.description: Madumarov resigned as leader of the Butun Kyrgyzstan parliamentary faction; deputy Iskhak Masaliev was elected as the new faction leader
recent_events.impact: Faction leadership transition; Madumarov retained party chairmanship

Current ruling party led by President Sadyr Japarov; main political rival of Butun Kyrgyzstan

core_business: Kyrgyz nationalist opposition political party advocating Kyrgyz ethnic priority, protection of labour migrants abroad, and a presidential system of government. Originally founded to support Kyrgyz migrant workers in Russia. The party is strongest in southern Kyrgyzstan. Party motto: Yyman! Myyzam! Tazalyk! (Faith! Law! Purity!)
apec_stance: As a Kyrgyz nationalist opposition party, Butun Kyrgyzstan's foreign policy focus centres on Kyrgyz sovereignty and regional security in Central Asia, including economic cooperation with Russia and China. The party's faction leader Iskhak Masaliev publicly advocated openly supporting Russia in its confrontation with Ukraine. The party's ethnonationalist stance makes it cautious about foreign investment and regional cooperation, emphasising protection of Kyrgyz national sovereignty and ethnic interests. Kyrgyzstan is not an APEC member but participates in regional forums; the party has not issued detailed APEC-specific positions.

collection_meta.notes: Enriched profile: added social accounts, departments, recent events, related entities, key people details. Party founded 2006-12-01, registered 2010. Currently 6/90 seats in Jogorku Kenesh.
